description: Gold labels for claim-level verification. 37 claim-citation pairs from a 43-source review of creatine and cognition, adjudicated against fetched evidence and machine-checked (quotes verified verbatim; numeric anchors enforced). v2 (2026-09-02): re-adjudicated under the v0.4.2 rubric — a multi-element sentence is partial when any element (a dose, a duration, an adjustment, a second finding) is not quotable at the stored evidence tier; 10 pairs moved from supported to partial (C001, C004, C005, C012, C016, C022, C025, C030, C032, C034), each with a note naming the uncovered element. Use with: verify_claims.py score --audit <candidate> --gold this-file; a judge configuration is trusted on a real review only at >= 80% agreement.

adjudications.note: the abstract reports intersubject variability (3.5-13.3%), not the sentence's marked regional variation; it averages across regions instead, and 20 g/day is the reviewer's 4 x 5 g
quote: Oral consumption of 4 x 5 g creatine-monohydrate/day for 4 wk yielded a statistically significant increase (8.7% corresponding to 0.6 mM, P < 0.001) of the mean concentration of total creatine (tCr) when averaged across brain regions and subjects (n = 6)
The data revealed considerable intersubject variability (3.5-13.3%)

claims.claim: In six healthy adults taking 20 g/day for four weeks, proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy detected a mean cerebral increase of 8.7%, with individual responses from 3.5% to 13.3% and marked regional variation.

adjudications.note: supports 'modest'; region-dependence not stated in this abstract
quote: research has shown that creatine supplementation can induce increased brain concentrations of creatine, albeit to a limited extent

adjudications.note: supports modest/inconsistent; region-dependence not explicit at abstract tier
quote: There is evidence that CrS increases brain creatine, but this response may be dose and/or duration dependent

claims.claim: Reviews of later imaging studies reach the same general conclusion: brain creatine is modifiable, but increases are modest, region dependent, and inconsistent across protocols,.

quote: vegetarians and omnivores had comparable brain total Cr content

claims.claim: Vegetarians consume little preformed creatine and commonly have lower muscle stores, yet a spectroscopy comparison found similar posterior-cingulate brain creatine in vegetarians and omnivores despite a large difference in dietary intake.

adjudications.note: the abstract states brain creatine content and cognitive performance in general; it does not say creatine was measured in three brain regions
quote: The sample comprised 67 healthy participants aged 10 to 12 years
a 7-day creatine supplementation protocol did not elicit improvements in brain creatine content or cognitive performance in healthy youth

claims.claim: A seven-day randomized study in 67 children likewise found neither increased creatine in three brain regions nor better verbal learning or executive performance.

adjudications.note: the seven-day duration and the 10% oxygen level of the hypoxic exposure are absent from this abstract text
quote: which increased brain creatine on average by 9.2%
Hypoxia-induced decrements in cognitive performance, specifically attentional capacity, were restored when participants were creatine supplemented

claims.claim: During hypoxia, seven days of creatine raised brain creatine by 9.2% and restored attention that deteriorated under 10% oxygen.

quote: creatine induces changes in PCr/Pi, ATP, tCr/tNAA, prevents a drop in pH level, and improves cognitive performance and processing speed

claims.claim: During overnight sleep deprivation, acute high-dose creatine altered cerebral high-energy-phosphate measures while attenuating deterioration on selected tasks.

quote: it bordered on significance for BDS (p = 0.067
was 0.09 for RAPM and 0.17 for BDS
we included eight exploratory cognitive tests
There was no indication that creatine improved the performance of our exploratory cognitive tasks

claims.claim: The backward-digit effect was small and uncertain (Cohen's d=0.17; p=0.067), matrix reasoning changed by d=0.09, and eight exploratory tasks showed no benefit.

quote: Twenty-two subjects (21+/-2 yr) ingested creatine (0.03 g/kg/day) or placebo for 6 weeks
There were no significant effects of group, no significant effects of time, and no significant group by time interactions for RT, CS, CSD, LRS, MP, RM, and MR

claims.claim: A six-week trial in 22 rested young adults found no group difference across seven tests of reaction time, substitution, reasoning, mathematical processing, and memory.

adjudications.note: oxygenation showed only a nonsignificant trend (p = 0.06), consistent with the claim
quote: thirty (M = 11, F = 19) participants were evenly randomized to receive supplementation with Cr (CR10:10 g/day or CR20:20 g/day) or a placebo (PLA:10 g/day) for 6 weeks
Creatine (independent of dosage) had no significant effect on the measures of cognitive performance

claims.claim: A six-week dose-response trial in 30 healthy young adults found no improvement with either 10 or 20 g/day in memory, attention, processing speed, or prefrontal oxygenation.

quote: dietary supplement of creatine (8 g/day for 5 days) reduces mental fatigue when subjects repeatedly perform a simple mathematical calculation
task-evoked increase of cerebral oxygenated hemoglobin in the brains of subjects measured by near infrared spectroscopy was significantly reduced

claims.claim: Five days of 8 g/day reduced reported mental fatigue during repeated calculation and changed task-evoked cerebral oxygenation.

quote: 14 physically active men ingested 20 g/day of CrM or placebo (PL) for 7 days
improved cognitive performance on the DCT (d = 0.77; p = 0.013)
cognitive function was evaluated using the digit cancellation test (DCT)

claims.claim: Seven days of 20 g/day improved one digit-cancellation measure in a crossover study of 14 active men, but it also tested sleep, exercise, soreness, and recovery outcomes.

adjudications.note: the paper reports the Stroop gain for the co-ingestion arm but never states that creatine nitrate alone failed, so the sentence's 'only' and the inference that the effect cannot be attributed to creatine are the reviewer's, not the source's
quote: twelve resistance-trained male athletes were supplemented with 7 days of creatine nitrate (5 g/day), caffeine (400 mg/day), and a combination of creatine nitrate and caffeine

Creatine nitrate and caffeine that were co-ingested significantly enhanced cognitive function, as indicated by improved scores in the Stroop Word–Color Interference test (p = 0.04; effect size = 0.163).

claims.claim: A 12-person study reported better Stroop interference only when creatine nitrate was co-administered with 400 mg caffeine, so the effect cannot be attributed to creatine.

adjudications.note: NOTE: these are the original estimates; the authors' published reply (10.1093/nutrit/nuac111) corrected the overall effect to SMD 0.19 (ns) after fixing double counting
quote: (standard mean difference [SMD] = 0.29, 95%CI, 0.04–0.53; I2 = 66%; P = 0.02)

claims.claim: The 2023 meta-analysis estimated an overall standardized mean difference of 0.29, roughly three-tenths of a standard deviation, but statistical heterogeneity was substantial at 66%.

quote: Creatine supplementation showed significant positive effects on memory (SMD = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.18–0.44

claims.claim: The broad 2024 meta-analysis produced a similar estimate of 0.31 (95% confidence interval 0.18-0.44).

adjudications.note: same correction caveat as C013: superseded by the authors' reply
quote: Subgroup analyses revealed a significant improvement in memory in older adults (66–76 years) (SMD = 0.88; 95%CI, 0.22–1.55; I2 = 83%; P = 0.009) compared with their younger counterparts (11–31 years) (SMD = 0.03; 95%CI, −0.14 to 0.20; I2 = 0%; P = 0.72)

claims.claim: The memory meta-analysis reported no benefit in younger adults (standardized mean difference 0.03, 95% confidence interval -0.14 to 0.20) but a larger effect among adults aged 66-76 (standardized mean difference 0.88, 95% confidence interval 0.22-1.55); that subgroup had 83% statistical heterogeneity and derived from few studies.

adjudications.note: the six studies, the 281 participants and the memory/reasoning finding are quotable; the sentence's second half, that results in the other cognitive domains were conflicting, is not in this abstract text
quote: Six studies (281 individuals) met our inclusion criteria
there was evidence that short term memory and intelligence/reasoning may be improved by creatine administration

claims.claim: A 2018 review found only six randomized trials with 281 healthy participants and judged short-term memory and reasoning potentially improved, while other domains were conflicting.

quote: The Panel concludes that a cause-and-effect relationship has not been established between creatine supplementation and an improvement in cognitive function in one or more of its domains

claims.claim: The European Food Safety Authority's formal appraisal concluded that a causal relationship with improved cognitive function had not been established.

quote: subjects consumed either a placebo or 20 g of creatine supplement for 5 d. Creatine supplementation did not influence measures of verbal fluency and vigilance. However, in vegetarians rather than in those who consume meat, creatine supplementation resulted in better memory

claims.claim: In 128 young women, five days of 20 g/day improved memory among vegetarians but not omnivores, although vigilance and verbal fluency were unchanged in both groups.

quote: Creatine supplementation had a significant positive effect (p < 0.0001) on both working memory (backward digit span) and intelligence (Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices)

claims.claim: The 2003 trial deliberately enrolled vegetarians and found better working memory and reasoning after supplementation.

adjudications.note: claim's n=32 is the sum of the reported groups (15+17); dose 20 g/day = 5 g four times daily [numeric anchor missing]
quote: Group 1 (n = 15) were given 5 g four times a day of placebo for 1 week, followed by the same dosage of creatine for the second week. Group 2 (n = 17) were given placebo both weeks
Results showed a significant effect of creatine supplementation on all tasks except backward number recall

claims.claim: An early controlled study assigned 32 older adults to placebo or a placebo-to-creatine sequence and reported improvement on most number-generation, recall, and long-term-memory tasks after one week at 20 g/day.

quote: after 12 weeks (POST-12) and after 24 weeks (POST-24) of creatine supplementation and/or strength training
Neither strength training nor creatine supplementation altered any parameter of cognitive performance

claims.claim: Fifty-six older women were randomized across creatine, placebo, resistance training plus creatine, and training plus placebo for 24 weeks; creatine did not improve memory, selective attention, inhibitory control, or any other cognitive parameter.

adjudications.note: the quotable association comes from a bivariate (unadjusted) model, so the sentence's 'after adjustment' is not supported; the abstract text also does not give the 60-year age floor
quote: NHANES 2001-2002 round included a total of 1340 older adults
A bivariate model revealed a significant positive correlation between DSS scores and creatine intake across the whole sample (τb = 0.043; P = 0.02)

claims.claim: In 1,340 US adults aged at least 60 years, higher estimated dietary creatine was weakly associated with better digit-symbol performance after adjustment.

quote: Forty-two participants (32 females, 10 males; > 60 yrs of age)
There was a significant correlation between the forward Corsi ( r = 0.703, P < 0.001), reverse Corsi ( r = 0.715, P < 0.001)

claims.claim: In 42 older adults, dietary creatine correlated strongly with forward and reverse visuospatial span.

quote: Six studies were included, with a total of 1542 participants (55.7% female)
Two studies were double-blind interventions in which participants were supplemented with creatine monohydrate
none of the studies that examined global cognition using the Mini Mental State Examination reported an association46,48 or change45 with creatine supplementation

claims.claim: The 2026 aging review identified six studies and 1,542 participants, but only two were supplementation interventions, the intervention results conflicted, and no study showed better global cognition.

adjudications.note: the four attenuated measures and the 24 h timepoint are quotable, but the abstract text gives 4 x 5 g rather than 20 g/day and states neither the 19 participants nor the intermittent-exercise component
quote: They took 5 g of creatine monohydrate or a placebo, dependent on their group, four times a time a day for 7 days
At 24 h, the creatine group demonstrated significantly less change in performance from 0 h (delta) in RMG, choice reaction time, balance and mood state

claims.claim: In 19 volunteers undergoing 24 hours of sleep deprivation plus intermittent exercise, seven days of 20 g/day creatine attenuated deterioration in random-movement generation, choice reaction time, balance, and mood.

quote: the creatine group performed significantly (p < 0.05) better than the placebo group on the central executive task but only at 36 h

claims.claim: A related 36-hour protocol found better performance only on a complex central-executive task at 36 hours.

quote: single dose creatine (0.35 g/kg) or placebo during sub-total 21 h sleep deprivation
All 15 subjects completed the study

claims.claim: In 15 adults kept awake for 21 hours, a single 0.35 g/kg dose changed brain high-energy-phosphate measures and attenuated worsening on several cognitive scores and processing times.

quote: subjects received either 0.2 g/kg creatine or 0.2 g/kg placebo orally at 9:00 pm
there is still an improvement of up to 12%

claims.claim: In 29 adults, a lower single dose of 0.2 g/kg reduced deterioration on selected tasks by up to about 12%.

quote: 14 healthy participants (4 females, 10 males
after a 7-d creatine supplementation (CR; 20 g
Accuracy on the Stroop task was higher in CR compared with PLAC (+4.9%; P = 0.026)
Handgrip strength endurance was higher in CR compared with PLAC (P = 0.022)
MF impaired visuomotor response time (+4.4%; P = 0.022) and Flanker accuracy (-5.0%; P = 0.009) in both conditions

claims.claim: In a 14-person crossover study, seven days of 20 g/day improved prolonged Stroop accuracy and handgrip endurance but did not prevent fatigue-related impairment in a shorter flanker or sport-specific visuomotor task.

adjudications.note: the verbal-fluency gain at 6 weeks in 18 patients is quotable; the claim that the other neuropsychological tests showed no difference is not in this abstract text
quote: Eighteen (N=18) patients with bipolar depression

There was a statistically significant difference between the treatment groups of the change on the total scores after 6 weeks in the verbal fluency test, with improvement in the group receiving adjunctive treatment with creatine

claims.claim: A six-week adjunctive trial in 18 patients with bipolar depression found improved verbal fluency but no difference on the other neuropsychological tests.

quote: Twelve schizophrenia patients (DSM-IV criteria) were enrolled into a treatment study with creatine or placebo, and each treatment was administered for 3 months (dosage, 3-5 grams per day)
Creatine treatment was not superior to placebo in improving the scores of PANSS, CGI, or the neurocognitive measures administered

claims.claim: A 12-patient crossover study in schizophrenia found no improvement in symptoms or its cognitive battery with 3-5 g/day.

adjudications.note: the phosphorylcreatine rise and the null for cognitive function are quotable, but the muscle-strength gain the sentence also asserts is absent from this abstract text, which likewise never names fibromyalgia
quote: 16-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial was conducted
the creatine group presented higher muscle phosphorylcreatine content when compared with the placebo group (+80.3% versus -2.7%; P = 0.04)
no general changes were observed in aerobic conditioning, pain, cognitive function, quality of sleep, and quality of life

claims.claim: In fibromyalgia, a 16-week randomized trial improved muscle phosphocreatine and strength but not cognitive function.

quote: we investigated the feasibility of 20 g/day CrM for 8 weeks in 20 patients with AD
brain tCr increased by 11% (p < .001). Cognition improved on global (p = .02) and fluid (p = .004) composites

claims.claim: In a single-arm pilot, 20 patients received 20 g/day for eight weeks; brain total creatine rose 11%, and several cognitive scores improved from baseline.

adjudications.note: the cohort, the futility stop and the 4-year median follow-up are quotable; the 10 g/day dose is nowhere in this abstract text
quote: included 1741 men and women with early (within 5 years of diagnosis) and treated (receiving dopaminergic therapy) Parkinson disease
The trial was terminated early for futility
The median follow-up time was 4 years

claims.claim: In 1,741 patients with early treated Parkinson disease, 10 g/day creatine was stopped for futility after a median four years.

quote: placebo-controlled study of up to 40 g daily of creatine monohydrate
553 participants were randomized to creatine (275) or placebo (278)
Adverse events, mainly gastrointestinal, were significantly more common in participants on creatine

claims.claim: In 553 patients with early Huntington disease, up to 40 g/day failed to slow functional decline and caused more gastrointestinal adverse events.

quote: Side effects were reported significantly more often for creatine than for placebo supplementation (p = 0.002, RR = 4.25)
No patients discontinued the study due to an adverse event

claims.claim: In the 2023 healthy-adult crossover trial, negative side effects were more frequent during creatine than placebo (risk ratio 4.25), although no participant discontinued because of them.
